utility.notes: SCE's own 'Incorporated Cities and Counties Served by SCE' fact sheet (updated 3/17/2025) explicitly lists 'Baldwin Park' by name among the cities in its service area. Baldwin Park's own BPROUD program materials also confirm BPROUD 'is available exclusively to those residents and businesses within Baldwin Park that are currently served by Southern California Edison,' with SCE continuing to handle metering, billing, and outages.

value.name: Baldwin Park Resident Owned Utility District (BPROUD)
value.notes: BPROUD is the City of Baldwin Park's own Community Choice Aggregation (CCA) program (not Clean Power Alliance), begun serving customers October 1, 2020. Confirmed via an official City of Baldwin Park City Council staff report (August 17, 2022) covering BPROUD's 2021 Power Content Label, which names 'Smart Choice' as the default product and 'Green Choice' as an optional 100%-renewable-leaning tier, and lists a net-metering option for customers who generate their own solar or wind power.

county.notes: Baldwin Park is a well-documented Los Angeles County city ('Hub of the San Gabriel Valley' per its own city seal, visible in the BPROUD staff report letterhead); also listed under Los Angeles County in SCE's own service-area fact sheet.

permit_authority.value: City of Baldwin Park Building & Safety Division

permit_url.notes: General Building & Safety Division page — no dedicated solar-specific page was found on the city's site this session. The city's Municipal Code Chapter 156 ('Small Residential Solar Energy System Permits,' covering expedited permit review, inspection requirements, and fees) is confirmed to exist via search indexing, but codelibrary.amlegal.com returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch on every attempt this session, so its specific eligibility/fee/timeline provisions could not be verified and are not included in this record.

interconnection_url.notes: SCE's own Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page — a utility-wide fact already established for other SCE-territory records this session.

value.name: California SGIP - current category and budget check required
value.description: New applications and waitlist applications for ratepayer-funded SGIP budgets closed on December 30, 2025. New AB 209 applications have a June 30, 2028 deadline. The 2026 SGIP rate table publishes $3.10/W for solar and $1.10/Wh for storage in applicable Residential Solar and Storage Equity categories. Household eligibility and live budget availability vary by category and program administrator; check the official Program Metrics tracker before relying on an incentive.
value.eligibility: Eligibility varies by 2026 SGIP budget category, program administrator, property, income/pathway, project rules, and live funding availability.

battery_programs.notes: SGIP program data refreshed on 2026-08-26 from the official 2026 Handbook and live Program Metrics. Earlier locality records contained 2025 opening/availability language. This record does not assert household eligibility, reservation availability, or a guaranteed incentive; current category and program-administrator status must be checked before reliance.

value.name: Building Permit/Certificate of Occupancy Application (general form; includes a 'Photovoltaic Panels' scope-of-work checkbox used for solar submittals)

required_documents.notes: Municipal Code section 156.06 says the documents for an expedited small residential rooftop solar application shall be on the City's website and that the Building Department shall adopt a standard plan and checklist. As of 2026-10-02 the Building & Safety page links only the general Building Permit/Certificate of Occupancy application (which includes a 'Photovoltaic Panels' scope-of-work checkbox) and no solar-specific checklist, so this record uses that general form.

value: Call (626) 813-5265 or (626) 813-5267 to request an inspection; 24-hour notice is required
Inspections are performed Monday through Friday
inspection_steps.notes: This is the City's general Building & Safety inspection-request process (stated on the same general Building Permit/Certificate of Occupancy Application form used for all permit types, including solar); the City does not publish a separate, solar-specific inspection sequence.

timeline_days.notes: Municipal Code section 156.07(A) says that for an application meeting the City's approved checklist and standard plan, a permit shall issue no later than five working days from submittal. No such checklist or standard plan was found on the City's Building & Safety page, so that commitment is not shown as a verified timeline here.

value.program_or_pathway: Small Residential Solar Energy System Permits (Baldwin Park Municipal Code Chapter 156)
other_conditions: Applies to systems installed on one- and two-family homes of R3 occupancy
System must conform to all applicable state fire, structural, electrical and other building codes
Solar panel or module array must not exceed the maximum legal building height as defined by the City

eligibility_constraints.notes: From the code's definition of a small residential rooftop solar energy system (section 156.03). The code site notes it may not reflect the most current legislation; confirm with the City.

value.name: Building Permit - Photovoltaic System (Residential, AB1414)
value.unit: up to 15kW, plus $15/kW for each additional kW
value.notes: Per the City's FY 2025-26 City-Wide Fee Schedule (effective October 20, 2025), Exhibit A-1 Building Permit, Plan Check & Inspection Fee Schedule.

value.name: Building Permit - Photovoltaic System (Commercial, AB1414)
value.unit: up to 50kW, plus $7/kW between 51-250kW, plus $5/kW above 251kW
value.notes: Per the City's FY 2025-26 City-Wide Fee Schedule (effective October 20, 2025), Exhibit A-1 Building Permit, Plan Check & Inspection Fee Schedule.

permit_fees.notes: From the City's FY 2025-26 City-Wide Fee Schedule, effective October 20, 2025, the most recent City-wide schedule found. The Building & Safety page still links an older FY 2020-21 schedule that lists the same figures. Municipal Code section 156.08 says separate permit and plan review fees apply to residential solar systems, but the schedule lists only this permit line, so any separate plan-review fee is not verified here.

rebates.notes: No BPROUD-specific or City-specific solar rebate/incentive program was found this session; BPROUD's own materials describe net-metering and rate tiers but no separate rebate program.
